newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firms.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firms.

text.p: Swedish bond yields came off morning highs to end lower on Wednesday on the back of a significantly stronger crown and lower than expected April U.S. producer price data.
"The U.S. PPI figure was much lower than expected and this fuelled interest rates," a dealer said. The U.S. PPI fell 0.6 percent in Aprilbut market players had not expected a change.

Foreign players bought crowns, taking strategic positions and making the currency firm to 4.4700 against the mark from 4.5175 late on Tuesday. "Many have long thought the crown undervalued," a trader said.
The six-month T-bill rate fell one basis point to 4.17 percent and the ten-year bond yield dropped six basis points to 6.94 percent.

Bond yields opened higher on newspaper reports that the prime and finance ministers had a more negative view on EMU than they had offically said and that the central bank might set up a secondary unemployment and growth target.
But the prime and finance ministers dismissed the articles.
During the session, Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom said he did not see any need to change the repo rate, currently at 4.10 percent.
Market players will be looking at U.S. and Swedish consumer price figures on Thursday and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20.
